title: Agent-to-Agent Attack Chain (Orchestrator identity spoofing)
summary: As documented, a spoofed agent identity makes two agents perform actions that neither should allow alone. As implemented, the effect is an acceptance reply.

LC.rationale: The attacker's A2A message with a self-declared from field is POSTed directly to the Orchestrator handler and determines its security-relevant reply with no mediation. As implemented the handler returns a fixed acceptance reply and delegates nothing.
evidence_refs: As implemented by default: the handler returns a fixed reply (Identity verified. Granting requested access). It sends no message to the Worker, and the Worker runs nothing.

CP.rationale: The A2A handler answers only the latest message; there is no durable store or cross-session memory on this path.
evidence_refs: Other chat agents answer only the latest user turn. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1841-1848)

AP.rationale: As implemented, no code sends a message from the Orchestrator to the Worker, so the effect never leaves the Orchestrator component.
evidence_refs: No code sends a message from the Orchestrator to the Worker. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1711-1770)

RH.rationale: No evaluator, verifier, or reward channel exists on this path; the handler is a scripted regex responder with no proxy objective to hack.
evidence_refs: Each returns a scripted reply based on regex detection and a self-declared sender name. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:251-295)
In the default configuration no model is called.

ES.rationale: The A2A endpoints expose no dynamic tools or extensions; the Worker's file/network tools are declared only and never invoked in the default path.
evidence_refs: ToolBot fetch_url can make a live request to another DVAA agent port. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2079-2096)

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models the Orchestrator as an agent that trusts the self-declared identity, delegates a dangerous task to the Worker, and has the Worker execute file and network tools, i.e., delegated action sequencing under an agent's identity-based decision.
